NexFoto 32GB Large 15 inch Digital Picture Frame, Wi-Fi Digital Photo Frame, Wall-Mountable, Instantly Share Photos Videos via App or Email, Gift for Father's Day This digital frame is a really nice size for displaying your photos. It can store a lot of them, and it has a decent brightness so you can easily see them even in a brightly lit room. The plastic frame isn't the nicest looking in my opinion; it would be nice if they offered different color and style frame options. I will probably end up painting my frame- I haven't quite figured how I plan to do that yet, but I just want it to look less like modern black plastic.

The app is really, truly terrible. It's difficult to figure out, it will only upload a few files at a time, and it takes forever, so if you have a lot of files to load, take my advice and don't even bother with the app. Just put them on a micro-SD card and load them that way.

Navigating the onboard menu is difficult, and I didn't find the directions to be very helpful. I was eventually able to get it figured out, more or less. There are some things that just don't make sense; for instance, in the main menu you can set the slide show to display the time each photo is shown. However, this doesn't actually do anything as far as I can tell, because after setting it the images will still flash by at 15 second intervals (this seems to be the default) until you go into the menu for the individual folder you are showing from and set the time intervals there. And the time options there are different than they are on the main menu; for instance, the main menu allows you to set 1 minute intervals. The folder menu allows 30 seconds and 2 minutes, but not 1 minute. So I'm not sure what all that's about.

Once you get it set up right, the picture looks very nice. It has an optional sleep mode you can set, and it has a motion sensor function you can enable if you like, but what I really wish it had was an ambient brightness sensor so that it would dim itself when the room is dark, and brighten itself when it gets brighter. This would be such a huge upgrade, especially for bedrooms, or TV rooms, or anywhere else where you want it to be dimmer when it's dark and brighter when it's bright.

Ultimate Ears TripleFi 10 Noise Isolating Earphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer) This was one of the last Ultimate Ears earbud lines before Logitech bought the company which resulted in an immediate drop in product quality and increase in product price. Yes, these are still wired headphones, but the sound fidelity is unmatched, and instead of complicated noise cancelling algorithms this simply employs noise isolation to block out ambient sound. These headphones have been out of production for some time, but for whatever reason you can still find them NIB from many vendors. They charge about a little more than what cut-rate vendors charged when they were new about 6 years ago, but they were way ahead of their time and frankly nothing on the market in this price range sounds even close to this good. Plus, these original UE headphones (I don't evangelize anything UE after Logitech bought them) have a lot of great design features. The earbud units are modular, so if you ever destroy the leads, you can always replace them for $10. Also, the standard leads these ship with do NOT have the mic and volume/start-stop control on the leads, but you can buy them in various levels of quality for about $20-60 aftermarket and swap them out. It's money well spent if you want to make calls on them. Also, the lead up to 6" from each bud is cased in memory metal so they can be bent to shape and hold in place to are a comfy fit on he outside of your ears- great idea.

All around the best earbud headphones for the money, if you can find them!
text_fidelity_b: Ultimate Ears TripleFi 10 Noise Isolating Earphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Wall Outlet Extender Surge Protector - 6 Outlet Wall Adapter with 3 USB Charging Ports (1 USB-C, 2 USB A), Multi Plug Outlets Wall Mount with Top Phone Holder for Home, Dorm Essentail, 490 Joules There has been an unpleasant shift, from who is responsible for supplying the power adapters for USB powered appliances. And, for the number of simple household appliances that now require those adapters. I suppose that I can see the logic in it. Newer electrical devices now require lower power. Thence, adapters. At first, they came with the device, like cell phones were supplied with the wall adapters. Eventually, you had to buy your own adapters. Even now, you have to be careful in selecting an adapter. There are basic ones that only have 3 amps. Some have 5 amps or more. Some only split all their power between multiple ports. Some are 'smart' and provide all the amps needed to multiple devices. Now, that's pretty much the rule. You gotta do it yourself and you better know what you're looking for. Disappointment is more common than satisfaction, in this new game.

These outlet adapters from Mifusa probably wouldn't have been my optimum choice, had the listing been a little more informative. But, based on what I read and how it works, it will do well enough.

The six outlets are too close together for bulky plugs or those that have the transformers built into the plugs. The total amperage across all three USB ports is only 3 amps. So, don't look to power multiple USB devices efficiently. BUT, you CAN plug six AC (that's alternating current, not air conditioning) of a low enough power draw, and three USB powered devices, IF they will all fit in the MIFUSA device, and know that they also have surge protection, as indicated by the little green light.

One star being crap and five stars being spectacular, I rate these as being 'okay'.
text_fidelity_b: Wall Outlet Extender Surge Protector - 6 Outlet Wall Adapter with 3 USB Charging Ports (1 USB-C, 2 USB A), Multi Plug Outlets Wall Mount with Top Phone Holder for Home, Dorm Essentail, 490 Joules

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Express - HD Streaming Player It may not be a techie's delight, but if you are looking for a budget streaming device, this one fits the bill. First off it is quite small making it ideal for cramped or limited spaces like a vacation home or boat. It comes with a short, two foot long cable and a piece of two sided tape. It connects to your tv with the cable.Depending where you tv is located you might have to use a longer cable. I did and found that the tape is not just a nice idea, it is a necessity. the box is so small and most cables so rigid it flips the box off making it impossible to regulate with the infrared remote. Take time to position because while the tape adheres well it looses its stickiness after being removed and repositioned. The infrared remote must be in line of sight for it to work. The way around that is to use the app. The app works with both android and iOS. The app has a voice control which I found to be inconsistent and a private listening feature that lets you use your phone headphones and mute the TV.

Performance is mixed. navigating and launching is slow. Netflix in particular really dragged. but playing content was excellent with no lag or problems. the channel selection is good with pretty much everything you would want available.

This is not bad for a budget streamer. there are definitely downsides, the ir remote, the lack of speed, the need for a cable. but it does work and is small enough for travel. I am frequently on the road for business and this does expand the limited options of hotel televisions. If you are on a budget and don't need or want the features that are available on pricier models this low end streamer will get the job done.
text_fidelity_b: Roku Express - HD Streaming Player

text_fidelity_a: Creative Pebble V2 - Minimalistic 2.0 USB-C Powered Desktop Speakers, 3.5 mm AUX-in, Up to 8W RMS Power for Computers and Laptops, Type-A Adapter Included and Extended Cable (Black) Okay, so the speakers sound and look great, especially for the price. Where I bump is product design... the power cord is EXCRUCIATINGLY short and runs out of the right speaker. So if you are running a setup where your computer MUST be on the left side of your desk (like mine) it may not reach your PC unless you cram the speakers dead center behind the monitor. That's what I had to do to get my cord to reach. You can buy a USB extender, but that shouldn't be a requirement for a product imo. Also the speakers is usb-c out which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but keep an eye out for the included adapter in the box. It can be very easy to miss and is essential for the speakers to work (unless your computer has usb-c input, most don't)
text_fidelity_b: Creative Pebble V2 - Minimalistic 2.0 USB-C Powered Desktop Speakers, 3.5 mm AUX-in, Up to 8W RMS Power for Computers and Laptops, Type-A Adapter Included and Extended Cable (Black)

She has about 200 albums stored in her player cabinet and only God knows how many more, stored in large plastic totes. A lot of these albums are rare and collectable, fetching big money on the vinyl trading market. We will sit in her office/nest talk, and just listen to music.

There is something about music recorded on vinyl. No, it's not the best medium for the purest sound. But, it DOES have a quality to it that has been lost to all the new tech out there. It's warm, rich and even the little pops and clicks you hear from well worn records is somehow comforting.

This little record cleaning kit helps us preserve the quality of the records and the music on them. It's simple, easy to use and worth every penny. We clean every record before we play it. And, using the included gel, we clean the stylus at the beginning of every session. Good purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
Monster ScreenClean Soft Touch Wipes, Screen Cleaner Wipes for Computer Screens, TV, Phones, Tablets, and Car Touch Screens, Home Office, 70 Count After 40-some years on the technical side of electrochemical fabrication (12" wafer fab) and manufacturing that included the IBM PS1 & PS2 birth … cleanliness is Godliness. I've likely tried every chemical variant of cleaner ever invented, though many fewer are now permitted for USA use.

Though impractical for the laptop, some excellent cleaners in the $1000/gal category might be suggested for cleansing strategic missile-related monitors and surfaces. The value and reliability of what device you are cleaning is the most critical consideration when choosing a cleaner. A wrong choice might pay back immediately with bad results, dissolving the anti-reflective coating or lamination of the touch screen overlay, removing specialized keyboard paints, ruining distinctive finishes, etc. For another, that same choice might do a bang-up job on the big screen at home, but when used on a laptop, it slowly dissolves and/or corrodes critical interconnects as you pass through dewpoints on that 17-hour airplane ride to Sydney.

Q: What is the best cleaner to shine on my $1500 laptop?

A: Not the cheapest $4/qt cleaner. Not one of grandma's window elixirs.

Behind the scenes, there is likely no other technical discussion as critical as cleaning and cleaners. Billions are spent every year on the problem. What I know from experience is that an alcohol solvent-based cleaner does a pretty good job erasing the symbology that makes my lighted keyboard legible. I look for a cleaner to remove the latent crusty-goo residue left by that anti-viral covid computer cleaner six months ago. Some cleaners with notionally benign saponifiers that sell under the enviro-friendly, "Green!", "non-GMO!" moniker is known to corrode solder joints and electro-plating to short the keyboard and LCD/OLED out.

Finding the right balance between solvent and saponifiers has not evolved smoothly. Saponifiers remove organics. The stuff that sprays out of your mouth and nose when yelling at the laptop. Solvents remove inorganics like hand cream, french fry grease, and Cheeto dust. I've rolled up all of this wisdom in my 'Rule #446 - Do not buy the cheapest electronics cleaner. Ever.'

This Monster cleaner is not cheap. It's a premium cleaner under a known premium brand. Given Monster brands, cleaning processes are the #1 priority for their established long-lived high-fidelity interconnection. My laptop has a touch screen that demands a non-delaminating cleaner and a lighted keyboard with that funky paint and laser-etched symbology. This Monster cleaner did an unexpectedly quick, no-smudge job on the laptop. All is good.
text_fidelity_b: Monster ScreenClean Soft Touch Wipes, Screen Cleaner Wipes for Computer Screens, TV, Phones, Tablets, and Car Touch Screens, Home Office, 70 Count

text_fidelity_a:
Izzo Swami Watch Golf GPS Overall, this is a very nice golf GPS for the price. I was a little worried about it being too complicated to use, but the manual explains all the features in reasonably good detail. I found it helpful to keep the manual with me the first couple of times I used it on the course to refer to, but after a few outings I felt comfortable using it.

I had an initial problem with the battery life in that it quit on me after about an hour of use. After leaving it in the charging cradle overnight, the next time it maintained its charge for a full afternoon's use. I've used it (and recharged it) several times since then and have had no problems, so it seems the first time was just a momentary glitch (or perhaps I didn't seat the charging cable firmly enough).

I very much like that it does not require a subscription to use, nor does it need to be tethered to a PC for the initial setup. It has a pretty extensive database of courses (Izzo says on their website that they cover 90% of the courses in the US). You can use their website to look up a course to see if it is included in the database.

Sat acquisition times is quick - took only a few minutes to get a lock and find my course the first time I used it. Acquisition time was even faster on subsequent uses. It uses a SiRF Star III receiver.

The display is clear even in sunlight, but it is a bit small for me. I don't usually have my reading glasses with me when I'm outdoors, so seeing the distance numbers took quite a bit of squinting. Granted, if you don't have aging eyes you won't find that to be a problem, but it would have been nice to have a larger display.

I also didn't find it all that comfortable to wear. It is lightweight and not too thick, but the strap was not very comfortable. Plus the greenish/yellow accent color (found on the inside of the strap and the sides of the unit) didn't appeal to me much - rather garish looking to my eye.

The warranty is only 90 days, which I think is too short given the price -- a year would be more appropriate.

But those are minor quibbles. Overall, the functionality is great - quick to acquire sats, accurate distances and straightforward to use. Considering the price of other brands, such as Garmin, this is a great value. Definitely should be on the short list if you're shopping for a golf GPS.

[As an aside, it's a real bear to the product out of the clamshell packaging. I didn't' factor that into the rating, but set aside some time to wrestle it out of the plastic jail it comes in should you buy one.]
text_fidelity_b: Izzo Swami Watch Golf GPS

Roku N1100 HD Media Player (Old Model) I've been researching ways to increase my cable channel happiness and reduce the costs. My research started a while ago, but a Cosumerist post about subscriber fees really got my goat. Look at all the junk channels that we are forced to pay for. I could care less about any sports channel or 90% of everything else. It is my opinion that we should be able to choose extra channels separately after we hook up with basic cable. You'll also notice that BH charges extra for a special HD tier. Sure it's only $6 a month, but geez, look how much markup there is. Anyways, you get the idea. I don't have any issues with BH. They've served me well for a few years. But I need more of what I want. Not what BH thinks I want.

So, I dropped down to basic cable and purchased a Roku HD unit. Set-up was a snap. I used HDMI for the TV and stream with a N router.

OMFG! This thing is amazing! In short, it streams unlimited Netflix offerings to your TV. The cheapest Netflix subscription ($9) is all you need. Plus it streams Amazon Video On Demand, and a bunch of internet channels. You can stream wirelessly or hard wire with an ethernet cable.

Can you tell I'm excited? Anytime I can boost my entertainment for less dollars is always a good day. The Roku will pay for itself in 2 months after switching to basic. And its HD!

Sigh...I must go.

I've been watching the original Dr. Who from the 60's.

1080P CAM/16GB SD CRD BLK It's always a good thing to be able to monitor your home and your pets while you're away.
Having this EZVIZ video camera, it can't get any easier.

Have been using a different video device for the past year. So wanted to see how this one compared.
Very easy set up. Using the quick set up guide, can have this up and running within a few minutes including downloading the needed app.
Long power cord with this. Can easily plug it in and have enough cord for it to reach a much higher level. Right now I have mine on a small shelf on the wall. If I choose to run it to the ceiling, (sticky pad included to do this) I will definitely get a nice cord cover to hide the cord that would be hanging down the wall to the outlet.
I like that it has audio so I'm able to talk and listen to whoever is in the room. Has nice night vision and was able to see the room when I only had a small night light on.
Video quality is really nice and clear. And love the wide angle with this. I can actually see the entire room.
Because I have animals, I have decided not to activate the motion detection. I really don't need alerts, to my phone, every time a dog moves around.
It's nice that I can buy a larger SD memory card for this. I will probably just increase it to 64GB. I really don't want to pay for cloud service so opted out of buying that.
No updates yet so not sure how well the "one-click updates" will work. But, if it works, it will be fantastic adding new features and functionality with just one click.
This is my first EZVIZ security camera but will love letting me see all of my EZVIZ cameras in one place if I choose to buy some more.

Great video security camera, for a decent price, that will definitely get used a LOT.
Would love to expand and eventually have my whole house monitored.
text_fidelity_b: 1080P CAM/16GB SD CRD BLK

text_fidelity_a:
Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier I've had problems with Pixmas in the past, mostly having to do with wireless networks and having to reinstall the software over and over to try to get them to hang on to network settings. I can't guarantee that this printer is going to be any better in the long run, but the set-up actually works pretty well if you use the standard version, not the WPS... and I'm getting way ahead of myself on this one.

To begin with, the printer requires a lot of time for set-up. You're not going to be doing this on the fly, so set aside an hour or so to: 1) remove all the tape of which there is much, 2) read over the instructions 3) install the ink, 4) run a print alignment 5) set up your wireless connection (about which more in a moment) 6) install the software (which takes a good 15 minutes or more), and 7) put the machine (and yourself) through its paces. Yeah, it's going to take a while.

Now I know you can read about the features on your own, so I'm here to tell you about the things that work for me and those that don't. First off, the wireless set-up is confusing. Choose Standard instead of WPS and save yourself some headaches unless you're a computer whiz kid. After the third error message in the WPS set-up I went to standard, entered my pass code and had the connection up and running in about a minute.

Once that was done and the software was installed I fired up the Canon Image Garden. First I scanned an image and attempted to rotate, crop and fix any deficiencies I found. The scan was over sharp and looked a bit jagged, but a little fiddling with the Canon software fixed that. Canon software also rotated and cropped perfectly. One really nice feature is that they remind you to put the printing side of the paper down in the paper cassette. How many pieces of paper will that save?

The biggest complaint I had was that it didn't give me a choice of which paper cassette to use for printing, so I got a ridiculously truncated image on the first try. I believe it chooses the paper based on the size of the image, which I get, but at the same time that limits flexibility in printing. I opened another photo processing program and it allowed me to print from whatever cassette I liked. Coupled with a better suite of applications for correction and enhancement, I think it's safe to say that I'll be using the Canon software almost never.

Printing on plain paper is clearly not going to be as satisfactory as it is on glossy, but in some cases I found it surprisingly good, good enough to give you an idea of what sort of image you're going to end up with when you switch to photo paper. It's also more than good enough for printing out emails and web pages.

Scanning and printing are both pretty fast, another plus. And the copy function works pretty seamlessly without any sort of computer interface. Just punch a couple of buttons and Bob's your uncle! It does take a bit of time to warm up and is a little noisy but no more so than any Canon printer I've ever used. It's not bothersome, in my opinion. You might feel otherwise.

Inks are easy to install, but you'll find refills pricey, no question. I suspect off-brand ones are available or will be soon enough.

In short, it's a good, inexpensive printer for a home or home office. Use photo paper and settings and get the full quality the MG5420 is capable of producing; I think it's pretty remarkable. The photos I printed out are as good as or in one case, better than the original. That's a powerful recommendation in my book.
text_fidelity_b: Canon Office Products MG5420 Wireless Color Photo Printer with Scanner and Copier

The results are phenomenal. I'm now booting up in 20-30 seconds instead of 2-3 minutes. Programs like Word and Excel come up so fast (without any associated services running full time in the background) that you barely see the splash screen. Lepow Portable Monitor - 2023 C2 15.6 inch FHD 1080P Portable Display with IPS Screen, Foldable Kickstand, Dual Speakers, Type-C HDMI Mini DP Port for Laptop PC Phone Xbox Switch PS5, Iron Gray First off I was a little irate with this product. I was so excited when it arrived today, that I was tracking Amazon. Okay upon opening this monitor the packaging was done right. Everything you need is in the box.

I am a coder and I needed this monitor to work perfectly with my Macbook Pro 2020 version.
This is from my experience others may have not experiences the trails and frustration I dealt with. I was seriously debating on returning it to the UPS store.
I couldn't get the picture to work. I worked on it for about 30 minutes and started surfing the web. I came across a video and watched this guy plug it in on the left side and it worked. So it will help to read and look at the pictures in the booklet first.

To save you the hours of frustration I experienced with this product, I will give you the information you need for this to work minutes out of the box. If you want to read this instead of the book.

1. Plug the USB-C port into the left side of the monitor. (I did all the other ports except that one.)

2. Plug into your USB-C port and the picture will work. No stand by or black-outs unless you use all the other ports besides the one on the left.

3. Issue: How do you have more than one thing on the screen?
System preferences>display>arrangement (important!)
The white box in the arrangement tab above the box, that is your Macbook. The second box is your monitor. If you want the monitor on the right side, move the box without the white bar over to the right. The same goes for the left. Now drag that picture over to the side your monitor is on and Bam!!! Beauty!

4. Problem: You don't want to use the volume on the monitor you'd rather listen on your Macbook.
System preferences>sound>output>slide that over to MacBook Pro speakers and take it off that Z1 crap. (That took me a while too.)
Overall, after the stress and migraine, I endured trying to figure this product out. I will have to say it works perfectly for my needs for now.
You better bet your bottom dollar if I have one issue with this product I will be returning it ASAP! Spending more than a hundred dollars on any product during COVID 19 is too much.

Overall I am glad I made this purchase and I'm glad I didn't take it to the UPS store to return it.
text_fidelity_b: Lepow Portable Monitor - 2023 C2 15.6 inch FHD 1080P Portable Display with IPS Screen, Foldable Kickstand, Dual Speakers, Type-C HDMI Mini DP Port for Laptop PC Phone Xbox Switch PS5, Iron Gray

text_fidelity_a:
Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth) The sound quality on this machine is amazing.

It is kind of hard to set it up. You use a microphone (included) to get the acoustics of the room. This is pretty normal. Then you have to set the sound field to match the source video or audio. That's not so standard. Denon, for example, can automatically detect what the source is putting out and adjust automatically. It took a while to figure out what lined up with what, but once I had it all sorted out, I was a very happy camper.

The range of audio, high to low, is very impressive. The bass is amazing. Naturally your speakers will play a role in this, more so than the receiver will, but with the right speakers this unit is pretty amazing. 7.2 strikes me as odd. There is only one audio channel that goes to the subwoofer, so the same sound is sent to both. Humans can't audiolocate subsonics, so there isn't much surround quality involved.

It supports both WiFi (with a good antenna that sticks up from the back) and Ethernet. As with any device, Ethernet will give you the more reliable connection.

It supports Blutooth, which is kind of cool. I use it to stream Audible books from my Kindle Fire. It's very easy to set up.

It supports passive HDMI, which is really nice. You don't have to have everything turned on if you don't need it. When the system powers itself down, which it does if it is inactive for two long -- say if you leave a video or disk paused -- the screen barely flickers.

It does not yet have support for Sirius, which is disappointing, but it supports other services, such as Pandora and, of course, Sony's own Music Unlimited service.
text_fidelity_b: Sony STR-DN1050 7.2 Channel Hi-Res 4K AV Receiver (Built-in Wi-fi & Bluetooth)

text_fidelity_a:
FULLJA WiFi Digital Picture Frame - 10.1 Inch Smart Digital Photo Frame with FHD IPS Touch Screen, 32GB Memory, Motion Sensor WiFi Electronic Picture Frame Share Photos and Videos Via App Email I don’t love it. This seems overpriced for what you get. For the price, I was expecting it to look more like a photo frame but instead, it kinda feels like an old monitor. My goal was to hang it on the wall during art shows with process videos playing. It will work OK for that but I’m disappointed that unless the video is in the exact proportion of the frame, it will always look a little “off” and there’s no means of changing how it’s framed in the display.

I think it’s at its best without the clock or any other additions.

The pros: It really does work right out of the box. It only took minutes to get photos onto it. The big screen is nice, I can see details in my photos. It is also bright with vivid colors. I like that it is flat which is why it performs better than an average monitor as a picture frame. The simple black frame doesn’t detract from its appearance. I like that there is an app and my husband and I were able to add photos, and I also like that there is a way to add photos via card in case software changes make the app obsolete. With the app, I was able to get videos onto it in minutes. I also like that it has a large amount of storage space and the means to expand it..

The cons: It is slow. I didn’t love the way the photos are displayed. I also hate the default animations because they are a bit cheesy. I want it to fade or some other non-intrusive way to change photos, and there is no means to edit it. The features are incredibly barebones. I hate that the default includes the time etc, I just want it to look like a photo frame! The audio is a bit tinny, much more so than a television etc. I also find it bizarre in 2023 to have an item that warns that it can destroy a USB if it’s removed without turning it off first…that seems like such an old-school problem!

I wish the plug was white because the black looks bad against the wall, and I prefer a minimalist look.

For the price, I feel like this could be better. There are just so few options for customizing the display.
text_fidelity_b: FULLJA WiFi Digital Picture Frame - 10.1 Inch Smart Digital Photo Frame with FHD IPS Touch Screen, 32GB Memory, Motion Sensor WiFi Electronic Picture Frame Share Photos and Videos Via App Email

Crucial P1 1TB 3D NAND NVMe PCIe Internal SSD, up to 2000MB/s - CT1000P1SSD8 I tried this SSD out in an older desktop workstation PC running Debian Linux. I bought the least expensive PCIe adapter card I could find (around twelve dollars) to install it. Even though it has an SSD as the primary drive, the workstation only has SATA 1 and USB 1.1 and 2.0, so I'm used to relatively slow speeds. Once I installed the card and rebooted, the NVMe didn't show in the files list, but it hadn't been formatted. It showed right up in the Gnome disks utility. I benchmarked it immediately, and, wow. Those speeds may not look like much to those who have later gen equipment, but the speeds were impressive for this older system.

It looks like I could have made it my primary drive, but I think I would choose to use this SSD as a personal cloud storage device in a USB enclosure. But enclosures for this particular 2280 (22mm X 80mm) form factor and NVMe are still rather pricey. I'm guessing the prices will come down eventually. Until then, the more economical option is to get an inexpensive adapter card and install it in a desktop PC, or install it in a laptop that has an M.2 slot and will accommodate 80mm long cards.

It looks like a good way to get some fast speeds and big capacity into some older gear. I'll leave the more technical reviews for the more technically minded.
text_fidelity_b: Crucial P1 1TB 3D NAND NVMe PCIe Internal SSD, up to 2000MB/s - CT1000P1SSD8

PHILIPS Active Noise Cancelling Headphones Wireless Bluetooth H6506 Flat Folding Lightweight Over Ear Wireless Headphones w/Multipoint Bluetooth Connection 30h Playtime with Deep Bass for Home/Office They did a quality job on these. Luxury without excess. Packaging is acceptable. The case feels great, the zipper is awesome. The headphones fit in very easily, and there is a mesh pouch inside for accessories.

The headphones have a giant L and R printed on the interior foam, which is convenient to figure out which way to put them on, but isn't visible once they are. The buttons are easy to access, labeled, and simple enough to remember.

Bluetooth was easy to connect and had audio cues.

I'm usually not a fan of gesture controls, but they work really smoothly and intuitively here.

The product itself feels high quality, and they're very comfortable and secure. Noise cancellation is fine, and a nice addition, but I don't find it notable. What was more impressive to me was just how little I noticed the usual irritations of wearing headphones. They don't have a background noise at all, they don't feel like they're going to fall off if I bend over or make a sudden move, they don't press uncomfortably, and they don't make noise when I turn my head.

I've tried a few modern wireless noise cancelling headphones, and I'd say some of the others win in one feature or another, but these are an excellent complete package.

LeadsaiL Wireless Computer Mouse, 2.4G Portable Slim Cordless Mouse Less Noise for Laptop Optical Mouse with 4 Buttons, AA Battery Used, USB Mouse for Laptop, Desktop, MacBook Great shape, very much like the classic and ubiquitous Logitech. I like that the pairing device is on-board. Lightweight and simple, a mouse is important for me if needing to get serious work done, especially anything with CAD or Visio.

The big question you need to ask yourself is, do you want a Bluetooth version or one like this that has its own receiver. It seems to me that if you always use this with the same computer and you have Bluetooth built in to the computer, then you probably want Bluetooth. Conversely, if you want this to use with multiple computers and/or you don't have Bluetooth built in to any one of the computers you will use the mouse with, then you'd want something like this. This is because pairing is easier in a case such as this, and drivers usually aren't an issue. Bluetooth usually isn't an issue either, but it might get irritating with frequent changing of machines. At least that is my experience.

Does not come with a carry bag, surprisingly. Mouse roller also functions as a button, as it should. It has an on/off switch on the back, which is nice for saving battery life and being able to leave this hooked up to a permanent install (although with a permanent desk setup, I personally stick with wired).

SAMSUNG 870 QVO SATA III SSD 2TB 2.5" Internal Solid State Drive, Upgrade Desktop PC or Laptop Memory and Storage for IT Pros, Creators, Everyday Users, MZ-77Q2T0B I was immediately suspicious of the box when I saw it.

It looked like the security tape had been lifted and then reapplied as can be seen in the photo I included with this review.

This was an item sold and shipped by Amazon.

I went online to watch unboxing videos of the same product so that I might be able to spot signs of a fake product when I opened it.

I called Amazon and verified that I could return the product for a refund even if opened and then took an unboxing video of it while on the phone with an Amazon rep.

I couldn't tell from looking at the drive or the rest of the packaging that anything was wrong with it.

I told the Amazon rep that I would check with Samsung the next next day to see if they could verify if it as an authentic Samsung serial number and as a new product.

I expressed my concern that even if it was a Samsung product that it might be used and I would never have any way of knowing. Or even if I could tell it was used after I installed it I would then be in the position of having to uninstall the drive in order to return it.

The Amazon rep told me that if anything was wrong with the product that Amazon would issue a refund without requiring me to return it if it was already installed in my computer.

Samsung verified the serial number the next day as being authentic and said that I could even tell if it had been used before as well by using their magician software program.

I thought the only way I would be able to detect if it was used was if there was old data on it left by someone else but Samsung said their software could detect if the drive had been written on before.

The catch is that that software can only be used to diagnose a drive after it has been installed internally to a direct SATA connection. Their software couldn't diagnose the drive through an HDMI connection to an external dock unfortunately.

Based on it having an authentic Samsung serial number, the assurance by Samsung that their software could detect both fake and used products and the assurance by the Amazon rep that I could receive a return-less refund if needed I went ahead and had the drive installed.

I figured the worst case scenario would be that it was a fake and/or non functional drive and I would have to take it out again immediately, the best case scenario was that it was a new and working Samsung drive and the in between scenario would be an authentic but used Samsung drive.

It turned out to be a used drive. It had been wiped and reformatted but it had been written to before.

I called Amazon back and told them the drive was verified as used and I expected a refund. At first the rep refused any refund and then said I would only receive a refund if I uninstalled the drive and sent it back.

I told them that was fine with me if they were willing to pay for both the installation and the uninstallation fees charged by a computer repair shop.

The Amazon rep of course refused either option so I directed him to get a suprivisor on the call and then played the recording of the conversation I had with the Amazon rep the day before....I got my refund immediately.

The big lesson here is to record the unboxing of any expensive items you buy, especially if the packaging looks tampered with or damaged.

Another lesson is to record your phone calls with Amazon reps or with any customer service person if you are calling up with an issue.

I learned a few things about this product and Amazon throughout this process.

These QVO Samsung drives store four bits of info per solid state cell. Most consumer SSD drives store only three and some expensive special purpose ones store just one.

These drives have a shorter life spans than three bits per cell drives and handle having large amounts of data written to them at slower speeds than three bits per cell drives. They should be cheaper as a result but often aren't.

Amazon has no way of tracking where a product comes from even if it was sold and shipped by them.

Amazon just puts all the Samsung 1TB 870 QVO drives into a bin regardless of whether or not Amazon bought them from Samsung directly themselves or they were supplied to Amazon by a third party seller.

Unless its an Amazon branded product that no one sells on Amazon but Amazon (Amazon basics, 365 Foods, etc) they have no way of knowing where it originally came from even if it is “sold and shipped by Amazon”.

Buyer beware.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 870 QVO SATA III SSD 2TB 2.5" Internal Solid State Drive, Upgrade Desktop PC or Laptop Memory and Storage for IT Pros, Creators, Everyday Users, MZ-77Q2T0B

text_fidelity_a:
Apple AirTag 4 Pack Honestly I was hesitant at buying these, having used Tiles in the past (disappointed). But these were lower in price than usual, so I bought some. IMPORTANT, you need at least one Apple device to set them up and use.
Short review: Awesome. Just buy them.
Longer review: Got them quickly and opens package and set up four of them. Took less than two/three minutes each. Pair with Apple device, (You can go in and personalize name, icon and a few others settings which takes few more minutes, but not hard or time consuming.)
I did two with an iPhone and two with an iPad. (I will try with my iMac when I add more).
I bought a bag of keyrings, I think twenty, of different colors, an a set of four wallet inserts. Love the keyrings, It takes some finagling, to get them in, not awful, just requires patience. Which I attached a set of keys to. Does not add a lot weight wise, and is noticable visually, and of course takes up some space, but nothing horrible.
The wallet inserts, is, ok. The size of a credit card, and is tapered across the wide side, going from one credit card thickness to twothree thick. There is a hole you put your Airtag and put it in your wallet. Just putting the Airtag your wallet makes big bump. Push come to shove it would work, but...
The wallet inserts adds some thickness to your wallet for sure, for me, not too awful. Not heavy, a bit heavier than a credit card. It works, but I am on the lookout for a better solution. I hear they have wallets made just for the Airtags, unless I can actually try one out, not ready for that debacle, or expense yet. (Anyone have tried one?).
These have come in handy already, someone grabbed the wrong keys and we were able to track them down a few towns over, honest mistake, we had theirs, they had ours. Misplaced wallet (fell out of workout pants) slid under car seat. Used play sound and tracking app, and found it pronto.
Plus numerous times set down in house, slid between cushions, fell into reusable shopping bags, someone picked up and moved them elsewhere in the house. Play sound, and or tracking app removes the stress and wasted time searching.
Getting ready for a long trip so I plan on dropping one in each suitcase and backpack.
It can be set to beep if it gets too far from your iDevice. Now this works best if you have an iPhone (or you never put your iPad down). So if at a restaurant, you set your keys down and walk away, you get so many feet, and it starts beeping.
There are a bunch of other accessories for the Airtag. A sticky sleeve, for say a laptop or tablet.
A friend even put one on her dogs, a new one likes to run away when she can ( yes they are working on training her, but in the meantime...).
If like me, you are a little flakey, and forgetful, these are awesome.
text_fidelity_b: Apple AirTag 4 Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder This is a good voice recorder. Whether you need it to record your voice memos, lectures, meetings, or discretely record your favorite spy, this will surely be a recorder you'll find many uses for.

It feels very secure in your hand, and has a comfortable feel and weight. It comes with a small pouch, which is nice. The record button is easy to find my sight or feel. The volume and forward/reverse buttons are on an outer button from the record button. Play and stop on the left and index and menu are on the right.

f1 and f2 buttons are primarily used for setting mic sensitivity and voice quality. Under Mic Sensitivity you can choose: Dictate (good for personal memos), Speech recognition (turns on when it hears voice), conversation (good for interviews or conversations, auto zoom (good for large areas where there may be close up voices and far voices), and lecture (good for lectures)

You can choose either low quality at 8kbps in Mp3 format to super high quality 192kbps in mp3. There is also a wave format in 1411 kbps. The higher quality you go impacts total record time. You can add a micro SD card for adding recording time.

There are also 4 index folders labeled A thru D. These are for separating projects. There is also a folder you could place music files if you wanted this to be a mp3 player.

There is also a menu setting where the voice quality and mic sensitivity can be accessed as well as numerous other options such as splitting files, display contrast, and clearvoice (an option that improves the sound quality of the recorded voiec)

The unit comes with rechargable AA batteries that will need to be charged when you first open it. They charge with the included usb to micro USB cord. Any other micro USB cord you own will also work. Once the recorder is connected to your computer through the USB cable you can download and upload voice or mp3 and wave files.

The only thing I wish this had was different settings for each index. For instance I would have liked to set index A for lecture mode at high quality, index B for dictate at a lower quality, etc. Once you set a mic sensitivity and recording quality, they are the same for all index until you change them in settings.

Overall a great quality recorder. Great for meetings, memos, and conversations.
text_fidelity_b: Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder

text_fidelity_a:
APC Back-UPS Pro 1000VA UPS Battery Backup & Surge Protector (BR1000G) I got this for Christmas and have only been using it for a few days now. I did have a problem with the set-up since there were no step by step instructions and you are left to figure out what goes where. I had omitted attaching the USB/phone jack between my old Windows XP computer and the UPS. I've used UPS's in years past, but they did not require a USB connection to a computer. I found out I had a problem when I was trying to install the software and it stopped loading and gave me a problem message, but no solution. I called the 1-888 number and without any fuss or waiting I got to speak to someone in the tech department who spoke very good English and solved my problem quickly.

I was tempted to deduct one star for the lousy (or total lack of) any instructions on how to connect this to your computer but didn't since the tech help was so good. There was a picture drawing instructing the user to remove the battery and turn it over so the green tape is on top which I managed to do alright. I don't hear any fan noise whatsoever as some others were complaining of. In fact, it's so quiet I can't even tell it's on unless I go and see the 3 LED lights on the top panel.

I tested it out a few minutes ago by turning off the power to the room that my computer is in. I was downstairs in the garage at the fuse box so I don't know if any beep occurred upstairs, but when I got there the computer was running off the UPS. Every 30 seconds I heard 4 beeps from the UPS telling me that it was being used as the power source. I only have my computer, monitor and modem connected to the UPS. I figure I don't need the extra peripheral equipment to stay powered up since it only sucks more energy from my UPS. I didn't wait to see how long the UPS would power my PC but I did sit there for about 3 minutes before I went downstairs and turned the power back on. My computer had a message on the screen saying that it was now being powered by regular current again (or something to that effect).

So far I like this UPS a LOT. There's nothing more frustrating then losing your work if the power goes off for only a couple of seconds. I edit a lot of music and it's not always easy or convenient to save it while I edit it just because of the nature of the program I use. So, I really like the idea of hearing my 4 beeps to let me know I might need to close out and shut down and not lose any work. I don't always have lights on so there may be nothing to tell me there's been a power outage except for the beeps on this UPS. There is a mute mode, but I need to hear the beeps.
text_fidelity_b: APC Back-UPS Pro 1000VA UPS Battery Backup & Surge Protector (BR1000G)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White) FM reception is flat out horrible where I live. It's like a radeo dead zone. My home theater system can pull in nothing. My stereo gets a lot of static. I listen almost exclusively online but I'd heard good things about this radio so I decided to give it a try. The reception was amazing. Perfectly clear. No static on FM at all. It sounds beautiful. The weather feed was full of static, but servicable--I ususally can't pull in the weather band at all. AM is average--neither the worse I've heard nor the best. But then, I don't expect much from AM.

It does the FM1, FM2 trick that some cars do. There is no difference. It just lets them repurpose the buttons. I find it odd, but not bad.

The only think I would have changed is how it hangs. If you don't have a shower hook (I don't) it hangs over the shower head. That tilts the entire unit forward. It should either suspend from the shower curtain rack (the strap is oriented the wrong way to do that--it would try to hand perpendicular to the curtain) or reach a better balance point. That's an issue of aesthetics, not function. I'd be worried about sitting it on the edge of the tub, as it is too likely to fall.

The one trick to remember, when sticking the antenna to the shower wall, is that suction cups don't work as well on a wet surface. Thoroughly dry the wall first, then place it. It helps will the issue of the antenna falling.
text_fidelity_b: Sony ICFS79W AM/FM/Weather Band Digital Tuner Shower Radio (White)

text_fidelity_a:
Large Print Backlit Keyboard, Quiet USB Wired Computer Keyboard, Full Size Keyboard with White Illuminated LED Compatible for Windows Desktop, Laptop, PC, Gaming, Black UPDATE: I'm changing my rating from 5 stars to 2 stars due to a rather quick failure of this keyboard. After only about 2 weeks use, some keys are non-functional (such as num lock -- it no longer works at all) and other keys are acting up (double entry when only pressed once). While the large labels and backlight design are great, the poor reliability, even for the low price, makes this a 2 star keyboard.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: This is an ideal keyboard if you find yourself squinting a bit to read key labels. The labels for each key on this keyboard are very large -- the largest I've come across. Additionally, it's backlit, allowing the labels to jump out even more.

The key action is decent. It's a bit clacky, but I've not had any issues with keys not properly registering. The backlight can be turned on and off with a single key. It also provides a number of useful shortcut function keys (accessed by pressing FN first, then the function key) such as vol up/down, play, mute, calculator, home page and others. I tend to not use them much (other than the Homepage and mute keys) but it's nice to have them be available.

It's plug and play compatible with Win 10. I plugged in the USB cord, Win 10 recognized it, and it was installed and ready to go.

The build quality is fine for a home keyboard but it lacks the durability for an office setting. Additionally, the backlight is not perfectly even (brighter at the base of the keyboard than the top). While these build quality issues puts my overall score at 4.5 stars, I'll round up since it does deliver its main benefit -- large, easy to read keys -- better than any other keyboard I've come across. Good value for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Large Print Backlit Keyboard, Quiet USB Wired Computer Keyboard, Full Size Keyboard with White Illuminated LED Compatible for Windows Desktop, Laptop, PC, Gaming, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Brainwavz M1 in-Ear Noise Isolating Earphones While these don’t offer the sound quality of higher-end Brainwavz buds (or higher-end models from other brands), the sound quality and overall performance is quite good for the price point, and the comfort is excellent.

The best description I can offer of the sound quality is “clean.” The upper and mid ranges come through very clearly and are far more well-defined than typical with budget/value earbuds. The bass is not pronounced. It’s there, but it’s not what I’d describe as punchy. These are not an ideal set if you’re looking for head-thumping bass.

The comfort is typical for Brainwavz, which is to say it’s excellent. There’s a variety of ear tips so you can customize the fit to your ear. I’m especially fond of the Comply foam tips since they provide a great (but still comfortable) seal. That helps maintain good sound isolation and also helps with the bass response. It also helps keep the earbuds in place while exercising.

The cords are thin but seem sturdy enough for typical use. The same for the ear buds themselves. While they don’t have as solid of a build quality as higher-priced models, I don’t get the feeling that these will be falling apart anytime soon. That being said, it would have been nice to have more reinforcement where the cord meets the earbud, since that’s a prime stress point in use (even though these come with a very well made carry case, more often than not I just wind them around whatever device I am using).

For the price these are hard to beat. Highly recommend these as a not too expensive way to substantially upgrade from the stock earbuds that come with many devices.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Brainwavz M1 in-Ear Noise Isolating Earphones

text_fidelity_a:
THINKWARE TW-X350 Dash Cam with 1080P Sony Exmor Sensor, Wi-Fi, & 2.7" LCD Screen Frustrating. Could not get the iPhone app to work at all, I'd slide the WiFi button to be informed that the WiFi was not functioning. Do I need to set up a local hotspot to use the WiFi feature to download the videos? Which appears to be about the only distinguishing feature of this dashcam. This is NOT a Sony product, apparently it uses licensed Sony technology. The dashcam itself is reasonably well designed. There's a horrid mechanical-female voice which I don't see how to disable. The user experience overall is poor. The manual is not bad as far as legibility, but the content is minimum. Minimal content in four or five languages.

The mounting scheme is atrocious, a joke. I'm not going to put self-adhesive cable anchors anywhere in my car, period. It's just plain dumb. I'm tempted to use a suction cup mount from another dashcam. Or cable ties on my rear-view mirror. But if you're homebrewing a solution right out of the box, maybe you're better off with another product altogether. The mounting suggestion is just a show-stopper. Not a good thing.

The video itself seems good, I mean, dashcams in general are fascinating and useful. But if you're expecting to have consumers put something in their car, it had been not involve defacing any part of the car or reducing its value. Leftover adhesive footprints would be an obvious problem.

I'm uploading a photo of the box. Green type on a black background. Not really a great design. Generally type and packaging tells you more about a product than the manufacturer might have intended. Just not that sophisticated.

Overall there are better dashcams out there. The ability to use WiFi to download video from the camera seemed promising, but I couldn't get it to work at all. The audio feedback from the device was far too loud and I couldn't turn it off. The mounting idea was dead on arrival, not happening.

Disappointing. Cannot recommend this product. A swing and a miss, as they say in baseball.
text_fidelity_b: THINKWARE TW-X350 Dash Cam with 1080P Sony Exmor Sensor, Wi-Fi, & 2.7" LCD Screen

The Incipio case does feel good to hold. It's the right size for the Paperwhite, and holds it securely, but the button is easy to access. I use it as a handhold, but you could tuck things into it as well. There's not a lot of padding to it, but more than my old cover, and that makes me feel more secure.

And it's nice to look at, very old-fashioned, and very much like an old hard cover book. I'm really thrilled to have it, and recommend the line, if not this particular case (tastes vary after all) to anyone looking for a decent Paperwhite cover.

I fully charged and connected to an ipad. the speaker played for 11hrs on about 35% volume. I did not try stamina mode. only a weenie would listen with no bass.
if you download the sony mobile software, you can tailor Bass-midrange-Treble with an equalizer screen. Greatly improves the flattened out default settings.
great for carrying in a golf bag or putting in a cupholder in a golf cart.
Cons:
its only around 8 watts. don't expect to rock out during a pool party or outdoor cookout.

the speakers are directional with the Sony logo. if you point the speakers away from your ears, the sound drops 20+%.
The bluetooth is a little glitchy when changing between sources but its not a showstopper. A reboot cleared up any failed connections with sony music center or bouncing between iphone and ipad.

I also bought a JBL Flip5 to experiment and compare to the xb23.

if anything changes for the good or worse, i will update my review.

text_fidelity_a:
HUION Inspiroy H1060P Graphics Drawing Tablet with 8192 Pressure Sensitivity Battery-Free Stylus and 12 Customized Hot Keys, 10 x 6.25 inches Digital Art Tablet for Mac, Windows PC and Android *UPDATED*
After a year of use. The tablet canvas started chipping in the middle of the protective coating. Stylus pressure and positioning still work but it's annoying as heck plus not it's even chipping more every time I go over same spot. I've never had that happen with any of the Huion & Wacom tablets I've owned for more years than this. I also can't seem to find a tablet protector for this either. So kind of bummed because I really like this...or want to really like this tablet.

*Original review*
First off, just like Wacoms these Huions are compatible with literally all major art software programs as well as budget programs.
I personally have used this Huion with Photoshop, Illustrator, 3D Studio Max, Zbrush, Mudbox, 3D Coat, Substance Painter, Clip Art Studio (Manga Studio), Krita, Painter, Paint Too Sai....can't remember the rest.
This NEW HUION 1060 PLUS is ASIN# B01FTE9HS2 and it comes with a stylus holder, 4 stylus nibs, a carrying case and drawing glove.
There is also another NEW version I saw on Amazon which includes 10 stylus nibs, holder and a glove without carrying case but they are the same exact tablet. They are both the same price on Amazon as of this writing.
Not to get you confused but there is an older one also called the 1060 Plus but it is not labled NEW or UPGRADED.
It is different cosmetically and has older technology and features.
The NEW 1060 Plus has Full-Area Surface Cover and Thinner Border, which makes the drawing surface bigger plus an attached side holder for stylus. Also, Quieter Express Keys, Better Linearity in art programs, Better pen pressure sensitivity.
(Specifications: Resolution: 5080 LPI, Report Rate: 233 RPS, 2048 Levels of Pressure, 10" x 6.25" active area.)
*Note: I just found out they released an even newer one with smoother pressure/linearity and has 8192 levels of pressure but it costs a little bit more.*

Now to the good stuff. Drivers were easy to install and worked right away; which is surprising because I've had driver issues with every non-Wacom tablets in the past. Actually, there are rare hiccups where the USB wouldn't recognize the tablet so I just have to replug back in. I've even had that issue with wacoms so I would just have to reconnect the USB back in to get it to recognize. Another common issue with older tablets (even Wacom) is that with Photoshop sometimes doesn't register the pressure sensitivity so I would have to either restart Photoshop or reconnect the USB.
But other than the super rare hiccups, this tablet looks very professional and is an great upgrade from the Huion H610 Pro, which I own, plus the Huion GT 220 graphics tablet which similar to the Wacom 22HD but way better IPS picture quality. I own the Wacom 22HD Touch and is totally not worth the $2000 I spent compared to the $700 I bought the Huion GT220 for. The Huion GT220 may have not come with express keys but I never use those awkward positioned keys anyways. I prefer the keyboard or game pad. I also owned a Wacom Intuos 2, Wacom Intuos 4 and an Intuos 4 Wireless which I've used throughout my professional career as an artist. (I wanted to compare them to see if a lower cost alternative is worth the savings). But my recommendation is if you are already an artist or aspiring to be an artist, don't hesitate on getting the tablet that gives you the best bang for your buck. Wacom does have good build but drivers can be flakey too. I've had some Wacoms stop recognizing the drivers to the point where I have to reinstall it.
With the 1060 PLUS you're pretty much set with a drawing tablet if you can't afford a Wacom or Surface Pro for all your 3D, drawing and painting needs. And to me, the pressure curve and sensitivity is feels equal to, if not better than, the Wacom tablets.

This Huion is the best bang for you buck for aspiring artist that want a professional tablet at the best price. I don't want to stray anyone away from a Wacom if they can afford it. But it's great to know that you can now save 1/5 the cost of a Wacom with the similar, if not better, specifications.
Actually, I purchased 5 of these for us artists at work and also had to recently recommend this Huion to my friends and family looking for a tablet for their kids that are also aspiring artist and animators. They showed me their kids' drawings and animation with the mouse I convinced their parents to get a drawing tablet. It is a must have for artists but you don't need to spend an arm and a leg. I truly believe this is the best $80 price range tablet on the market today that runs on Windows 10 (as of this writing). It has worked well for me for my professional (and personal) work with 3D sculpting, drawing and painting. Sorry Wacom....$250 to $300 for a comparable mid-size tablet is not aspiring artist friendly. They may look a bit cooler but they all achieve the same end. They also have Wacom Bamboos or budget Wacoms under $70 but they all lack the pressure sensitivity and features with only 1024 levels of sensitivity. I'm not a Huion salesman but this just makes sense and achieves the same end.....which is quality art without frustrating hardware and features.
text_fidelity_b: HUION Inspiroy H1060P Graphics Drawing Tablet with 8192 Pressure Sensitivity Battery-Free Stylus and 12 Customized Hot Keys, 10 x 6.25 inches Digital Art Tablet for Mac, Windows PC and Android

Canon EF 24-105mm f/4 L IS USM Lens for Canon EOS SLR Cameras The Canon 24-105mm f/4 L lens with Image Stabilization is a fantastic lens for those times when you just want to have one lens on the camera but you also want to have a lot of options with your focal range. The range on this lens takes you from a decent wide angle perspective to a mid-range telephoto without any light loss (the maximum aperture is constant throughout the zoom range) and image stabilization keeps focus problems due to hand shake well away.

Optical quality is excellent, as you would expect with an L lens, and autofocus is smooth and fast. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @40-170mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.

text_fidelity_a:
ContourROAM Hands-free HD Camcorder Picked up a couple of these when Amazon had them on sale for half price. Had to return one because it was out of focus; Amazon processed the return quickly and the replacement works great.

Very pleased with the image quality of these cameras in the 1080p mode (which I always use). The video quality is sharp and colorful. Make sure you use the camera software to set the image quality to the highest level for best results.

Sound quality is a mixed bag. This camera uses noise reduction to reduce wind noise (which is a big problem with older Contour cameras at even moderate bicycling speeds), but the noise reduction also severely muffles your voice if you are trying to narrate a video while filming.

The camera controls are very easy to use, which is an improvement over earlier Contour cameras. The instant-on feature works great if you're filming only pieces of your event. I get about 3 hours of video from one battery charge. That also seems to be the amount of video that fits on a 32GB microSD card. If your event is longer than 3 hours, use the instant-on/instant-off feature to switch the camera on for just the important parts. The instant-on feature is a nice improvement over earlier Contour cameras that are difficult to turn on when you are moving.

Contour cameras seem to go on sale more often than GoPro. If you can catch it at a good sale price, I think Contour is a much better value than GoPro.
text_fidelity_b: ContourROAM Hands-free HD Camcorder

My system (Win7) did not recognize the drive, but the included software, Samsung Magician, said the drive was there, operating properly, but was "frozen". I googled the malfunction and found out that the drive had no partitions.

So first step was to get in Disk Management, find the drive, click on the 113+gb unallocated space and create a partition.

Step two, reboot and change my boot sequence because Samsung Magician felt it was necessary to change it for me and made this new SSD my boot drive, even though it had no OS on it to boot.

Step three, change my power management plan back to what I had before because Samsung Magician felt it was better to change it to hibernate instead of what I wanted. I hate Hibernate.

After that it worked great. I use this SSD for games only because it's so damn fast, but I wish the included software and instructions were better, hence the 4 stars and not 5.

text_fidelity_a:
REOLINK 4K Security Camera Outdoor System, Surveillance IP PoE Camera with Human/Vehicle/Pet Detection, 25FPS Daytime, 100F IR Night Vision, Work with Smart Home, Up to 256GB SD Card, RLC-810A Fantastic camera. One of those items that screamed quality right out of the box. Good build, compact size, and has a waterproof connector for your Ethernet cable. Can be mounted where the cable comes through a hole in a fascia board behind the camera or where the cable comes out the side of the base. Base is infinitely adjustable. Camera has slight overhang on the top to keep water off the lens. Three pigtail cables - RJ-45 female connector can be the single cable if you have PoE or you can power this via a 12v power adapter or cable (local or centralized) for versatility.

This is my first IP camera, but I've used many analog cameras and DVRs.

I've hooked this up three ways: By itself, to a switch on the same network as a stand-alone NVR, and to a switch on the same network utilizing my QNAP NAS as the NVR - in each case powered by PoE. Here are some details I've figured out in the process:

---By itself: You can view it quickly and easily without delay with the App, which seems to have all the things you'd expect from a camera viewing app. I assume you can record to or snapshot to an SD card from the description, but I'm going to record to my network, so I didn't try that feature. This was just plug and play, worked super easy.

What I love is that once you figure out the IP address, you can access the camera via a webserver, which pretty much future-proofs the hardware. I despise "smart" devices where you need an app, because then you're at their mercy to run their app on whatever OS they decide to use and they can force you to make accounts, update, etc. Having this open to the user/owner is the way to go. Bravo.

And that web server is full featured. I was able to play around and do everything here before I bothered downloading the app.

Note that - like every camera I've ever used - the viewing software sends a substream which is lower resolution unless you demand the higher resolution. With the app you can see low and medium resolution, but 4k has trouble playing over WiFi (or else it's just smart enough to realize my screen can't support it anyway). Just pointing this out so you realize if you're seeing pixels, that doesn't mean the camera isn't actually recording at 4k.

---With NVR: I recently acquired a cheap 8-channel 4k NVR that I believe to be a Uniview OEM. I added a hard drive and put it on the same network as this camera. The NVR has an 8 port PoE switch built in, but it must also be a router, because it wants to use a different subnet if you put the camera on the NVR's switch. Otherwise, you can easily point the NVR to the camera via IP address.

So...if you point the NVR to the camera via IP address, you can view the camera from its own app or from the NVR app. I assume this still takes one of the NVRs 8 channels. This might be useful if you want to give someone access to just one camera on your network. But it occurred to me that, setup this way, you have constant data streaming over your network, and after you add quite a few cameras in 4k, this is going to start adding up.

If you put the camera directly on the NVR, you'll have to change the IP manually to match the subnet, or maybe you'll somehow get it to work through the NVR or with DHCP. I hadn't bothered spending time figuring this out yet because at the time I thought I'd just use my other switch, but I'm thinking once I get more cameras, it'll probably make more sense to put them directly onto the NVR and ...actually, then I won't have to change my entire IP scheme since I won't have so many new devices to organize.

I'm certain I can get it all working in unison with no problem, but it is more complicated than if you just buy an NVR set with a bunch of cameras already ready to work together. Either way shouldn't be a problem if you have IP knowledge, but I'm guessing a random homeowner might prefer a set.

---Using my NAS as NVR. Hmmm...a little disappointed with QNAP in this regard. I mean, I have three NASs, and I'm assuming they all have 2 licenses included, but to combine them into one program then I believe requires yet another license. I'm not into licenses, even if they're a one time deal, because that means you need accounts and if something happens where they're lost, you can run into all kinds of other issues. I just think consumers need to stand up to this sort of thing. But anyway, I had two included, so I tried it out:

I realized that this is a lot of work for my little consumer grade NAS, and even if I had a more hardcore NAS, I'm not sure I want resources being used all the time. It seems like I couldn't get it to use H.265 compression, nor could I get it to record at the higher resolutions and frame rates. Again, I didn't play with this too awful much once I got it recording and working because I already realized I definitely like the stand alone DVR better. The QNAP even had extra stuff to download and windows to pop up on your PC and all this other stuff. Just not as streamlined as I had hoped.

----Conclusion is that the camera is awesome. I'm not sure many are any better at this point. If you want something that just works easy and you don't know much about networking, you may wish to just buy an NVR set. But if you are IP capable, I think buying components separately could be a great way to go because you can really customize what you want to do. But as always, more options with networking means more potential headaches. But I am pretty certain that once you get it working the way you want it, you should be able to forget all about it and have it work indefinitely.

Oh, and after all that, I shouldn't forget to point out that I'd be thrilled to have this all by itself watching my porch just so I can tell when there's a package out there. My Ring (that came with the house) can't even see that because of the angle it is set at.
text_fidelity_b: REOLINK 4K Security Camera Outdoor System, Surveillance IP PoE Camera with Human/Vehicle/Pet Detection, 25FPS Daytime, 100F IR Night Vision, Work with Smart Home, Up to 256GB SD Card, RLC-810A

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle, 6" E Ink Display, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I'm a big fan of Kindle e-Readers. We own two of the older generation ones (the last Kindles with keyboard) and for x-mas I bought my mother a Kindle Fire HD 8.9 for x-mas. But, alas, she doesn't seem to have fine enough motor control to hit the small buttons on that device (see my review for that device). So the Fire has been sitting unused on the coffee table for a few months now.

But this is not a review of the Fire HD 8.9. I want to describe my very short experience with the basic Kindle and the Kindle Paperwhite - as they relate to the intended user: my mom. She recently suffered a stroke and one of the side effects is that she now has a constant tremble in her left hand. As she had trouble with the Fire HD 8.9 we went to Staples to see if the more purpose-built Kindles were easier to operate. We were not surprised when she often made mistakes selecting books on the Paperwhite's touch screen. But we were surprised to find that she couldn't even handle the physical buttons on the basic Kindle! From what I could tell, the problems were: the side-buttons (page forward/backward) are much smaller and narrower than they were on our old Kindles (which my mom had no trouble with), so basic navigation among pages became iffy. Similarly, the D-pad is smaller too - and that made selection of books difficult for her. Finally, while I could easily hold my old Kindle with one hand AND operate the page forward button, this is a bit more difficult with the new basic Kindle. My mom could not manage it at all. And since she can't hold the Kindle with her trembling left hand, neither e-Reader was for her. [She is now making do with the Kindle Fire HD 8.9 by laying it on a flat surface and only operating it with her right hand].

I'm still giving the Kindle 4 stars because none of these shortcomings are of interest to the majority of people, but I wanted folks to be aware of the newer devices' potential limitations with those suffering from limited motor skills.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle, 6" E Ink Display, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a: VIZIO M70-C3 70-Inch Class Ultra HD Full-Array LED Smart TV I really like this TV. So why 4 stars instead of 5? I think back to the 42 inch Panasonic Plasma that I bought in 2002 and cringe at the multiple thousands spent. This is a lot of TV for the money. The picture is great. Compared to hooking up a Roku the initial start up and response is much slower. Of course if you are going to hook up a Roku then this is no big deal. If you do not have viewing angle concerns and are hooking up a Roku then I think you will absolutely love this amazing bargain.
